standard.name: Minimum Information about a Molecular Interaction eXperiment (MIMIx)
standard.abstract: MIMIx defines minimum reporting guidelines for molecular interaction experiments (protein–protein, protein–nucleic acid, etc.). It is intended to guide authors and databases on which pieces of information to capture so that interaction experiments can be understood, compared, and systematically archived. The recorded data take the form of interaction metadata (detection method, experimental role, interaction type, controlled-vocabulary terms) and controlled-vocabulary definitions for interaction detection methods.

classification.rationale: MIMIx provides a checklist/collection of metadata items and controlled-vocabulary terms for reporting molecular interaction experiments (i.e., concrete metadata fields), and the supplied supplementary material includes explicit Controlled Vocabulary term definitions suitable for tabular representation.

purpose.name: MIMIx purpose / scope
purpose.descr: Short description of the guideline's intent and scope.
purpose.evidence: MIMIx is a community guideline advising the user on how to fully describe a molecular interaction experiment and which information it is important to capture.

publication_reference.name: Published reference
publication_reference.descr: Citation for the MIMIx guideline as published in the literature.
publication_reference.evidence: The MIMIx draft guidelines attached below, has later been published by Nature Biotechnology, Nat Biotechnol. 2007 Aug;25(8):894-8.

interaction_detection_method:MI:0004.name: affinity chromatography technology (MI:0004)
interaction_detection_method:MI:0004.descr: Controlled-vocabulary term for an interaction detection/affinity purification technology.
interaction_detection_method:MI:0004.evidence: "This class of approaches is characterised by the use of affinity resins as tools to purify molecule of interest (baits) and their binding partners. The baits can be captured by a variety of high affinity ligands linked to a resin - for example, antibodies specific for the bait itself, antibodies for specific tags engineered to be expressed as part of the bait or other high affinity binders such as glutathione resins for GST fusion proteins, metal resins for histidine-tagged proteins." [PMID:7708014]

interaction_detection_method:MI:0006.name: anti bait coimmunoprecipitation (MI:0006)
interaction_detection_method:MI:0006.descr: Controlled-vocabulary term for anti-bait coimmunoprecipitation detection method.
interaction_detection_method:MI:0006.evidence: "A specific antibody for the protein of interest (bait) is available, this is used to generate a high affinity resin to capture the endogenous bait present in a sample." [PMID:7708014]

interaction_detection_method:MI:0007.name: anti tag coimmunoprecipitation (MI:0007)
interaction_detection_method:MI:0007.descr: Controlled-vocabulary term for anti-tag coimmunoprecipitation detection method.
interaction_detection_method:MI:0007.evidence: "A specific antibody for the protein of interest is not available, therefore the bait protein is expressed as a hybrid protein fused to a tag peptide/protein for which efficient and specific antibodies or a specific ligand are available." [PMID:7708014]

interaction_detection_method:MI:0008.name: array technology (MI:0008)
interaction_detection_method:MI:0008.descr: Controlled-vocabulary term for array-based detection technologies.
interaction_detection_method:MI:0008.evidence: "In this class of methodologies, the molecules to be tested are presented ordered in an array format (typically at high density) on planar supports. The characteristics and chemical nature of the planar support can vary. This format permits the simultaneous assay, in controlled conditions, of several thousand proteins/peptides/nucleic acids for different functions, for instance their ability to bind any given molecule." [PMID:14755292]

interaction_detection_method:MI:0009.name: bacterial display (MI:0009)
interaction_detection_method:MI:0009.descr: Controlled-vocabulary term for bacterial display technologies used for interaction detection.
interaction_detection_method:MI:0009.evidence: "The protein of interest is presented on the outer membrane of Gram negative bacteria by expressing it as a fusion partner to peptide signals that direct heterologous proteins to the cell surface. For instance, a single chain Fv (scFv) antibody fragment, consisting of the variable heavy and variable light domains from two separate anti-digoxin monoclonal antibodies, was displayed on the outer membrane of Escherichia coli by fusing it to an Lpp-OmpA. Similar systems have also been developed for gram positive bacteria. Fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS), is used to specifically select clones displaying a protein binding to scFv-producing cells." [PMID:10436088, PMID:8248129]

interaction_detection_method:MI:0010.name: beta galactosidase complementation (MI:0010)
interaction_detection_method:MI:0010.descr: Controlled-vocabulary term for beta-galactosidase complementation assays.
interaction_detection_method:MI:0010.evidence: "Beta-galactosidase activity can be used to monitor the interaction of chimeric proteins. Pairs of inactive beta gal deletion mutants are capable of complementing to restore activity when fused to interacting protein partners. Critical to the success of this system is the choice of two poorly complementing mutant moieties, since strongly complementing mutants spontaneously assemble and produce functional beta-gal activity detectable in absence of any fused protein fragment." [PMID:12042868, PMID:9237989]

interaction_detection_method:MI:0011.name: beta lactamase complementation (MI:0011)
interaction_detection_method:MI:0011.descr: Controlled-vocabulary term for beta-lactamase complementation assays.
interaction_detection_method:MI:0011.evidence: "This strategy is based on a protein fragment complementation assay (PCA) of the enzyme TEM-1 beta-lactamase. The approach includes a simple colorimetric in vitro assays using the cephalosporin nitrocefin and assays in intact cells using the fluorescent substrate CCF2/AM. The combination of in vitro colorimetric and in vivo fluorescence assays of beta-lactamase in mammalian cells permits a variety of sensitive and high-throughput large-scale applications." [PMID:12042868]

interaction_detection_method:MI:0012.name: bioluminescence resonance energy transfer (MI:0012)
interaction_detection_method:MI:0012.descr: Controlled-vocabulary term for BRET/LRET bioluminescence resonance energy transfer assays.
interaction_detection_method:MI:0012.evidence: "In this variation of the FRET assay the donor fluorophore is replaced by a luciferase (typically Renilla luciferase). In the presence of its substrate, the luciferase catalyses a bioluminescent reaction that excites the acceptor fluorophore through a resonance energy transfer mechanism. As with FRET the energy transfer occurs only if the protein fused to the luciferase and the one fused to the acceptor fluorophore are in close proximity (10-100 Angstrom)." [PMID:9874787, PMID for application instance:10725388]

interaction_detection_method:MI:0013.name: biophysical (MI:0013)
interaction_detection_method:MI:0013.descr: Controlled-vocabulary term grouping biophysical experimental approaches.
interaction_detection_method:MI:0013.evidence: "The application of physical principles and methods to biological experiments." [PMID:14755292]

interaction_detection_method:MI:0014.name: adenylate cyclase complementation (MI:0014)
interaction_detection_method:MI:0014.descr: Controlled-vocabulary term for adenylate cyclase complementation (bacterial two-hybrid) assays.
interaction_detection_method:MI:0014.evidence: "Adenylate cyclase is encoded by the cyaA gene and contains a catalytic domain which can be proteolytically cleaved into two complementary fragments, T25 and T18, which remain associated in the presence of calmodulin in a fully active ternary complex. In the absence of calmodulin, the mixture of the two fragments does not exhibit detectable activity, suggesting that the two fragments do not associate. When expressed in an adenylate cyclase-deficient E. coli strain (E. coli lacks calmodulin or calmodulin-related proteins), the T25 and T18 fragments fused to putative interacting proteins are brought into close association which result in cAMP synthesis. The level of reconstructed adenylate cyclase can be estimated by monitoring the expression of a cAMP dependent reporter gene." [PMID:9576956]

interaction_detection_method:MI:0016.name: circular dichroism (MI:0016)
interaction_detection_method:MI:0016.descr: Controlled-vocabulary term for circular dichroism (CD) spectroscopy as a biophysical method relevant to interactions.
interaction_detection_method:MI:0016.evidence: "Circular dichroism (CD) is observed when optically active molecules absorb left and right hand circularly polarized light slightly differently. Linearly polarized light can be viewed as a superposition of two components of circularly polarized light of equal amplitude and phase but opposite handness. When this light passes through an optically active sample the two polarized components are absorbed differently. The difference in left and right handed absorbance A(l)- A(r) is the signal registered in CD spectra. This signal displays distinct features corresponding to different secondary structures present in peptides, proteins and nucleic acids. The analysis of CD spectra can therefore yield valuable information about the secondary structure of biological macromolecules and the interactions among molecules that influence their structure." [PMID:11578931]

standard.notes: Extracted fields focus on the Controlled Vocabulary terms for interaction detection methods provided in the MIMIx supplementary materials (Note 1). The original MIMIx paper (Nat Biotechnol. 2007 Aug;25(8):894-8) contains the full checklist of reporting items; only items with explicit verbatim text available in the provided materials were extracted here.
